title: Aider Operating Card
summary: Use Aider as a Git-aware terminal pair programmer with an explicit model, file set, test loop, and recovery checkpoint.
prerequisites: Python 3 available either as the python command or through the Windows launcher command py -3
Git available as the git command; the exercise uses repository-local identity settings and does not require or modify global Git configuration
Permission to create and delete a disposable repository under the current user's temporary directory
Optional only: approval to install or run Aider and either an approved provider credential or a running local Ollama service with an explicitly selected model

sections.title: Use it for a Git-centered terminal pairing loop
paragraphs: Aider is an AI pair-programming tool for the terminal. It edits files added to its chat and is tightly integrated with Git. This exercise first uses a completely runnable, no-model baseline. You will create a disposable repository, observe a failing Python standard-library test, inspect the defect, repair it manually, and verify the result. The later Aider path is optional, metered or locally resourced, and was not executed in preparing this card.

The exercise intentionally uses only Python's standard library. The unittest module supplies TestCase and assertions and can be run with either python -m unittest or, on Windows when python is unavailable, py -3 -m unittest. The setup verifies a Python 3 executable and Git before creating the repository. It refuses to continue if the selected directory already exists, uses repository-local Git identity settings, and does not change global Git configuration.

code.label: Operational card
code.code:
Task: Make factorial(0), factorial(1), and factorial(5) return 1, 1, and 120 without changing the tests.
Scope: A newly created disposable Git repository named aider-factorial-lab; only factorial.py and test_factorial.py may be edited.
Permissions: Local file edits, local Python 3 test execution, local Git inspection and commits. Optional model access only after explicit learner consent.
Model: None for the baseline. For the optional path, select either deepseek/deepseek-chat with DEEPSEEK_API_KEY or ollama_chat/<an already approved and locally installed model> with a local Ollama endpoint.
Conventions: Python standard library only; preserve the factorial function name; do not weaken, remove, or skip tests; do not add dependencies.
Verification: Review git diff; run the verified Python 3 command with -m unittest -v; require three passing tests; inspect git status and git log.
Test evidence: Initial boundary test errors with ValueError: n must be non-negative because factorial(0) calls factorial(-1), which reaches the existing negative-input guard. After repair, test_factorial_of_zero, test_factorial_of_one, and test_factorial_of_five report ok, followed by Ran 3 tests and OK.
Stop conditions: Stop on an existing target path, an unavailable Python 3 or Git command, unexpected files, a request for a secret, edits outside factorial.py, weakened tests, dependency installation, unresolved test failure, or a diff you do not understand.
Recovery: Exit Aider if open. Use /undo only when the last commit was made by Aider and you have reviewed what it will undo. Otherwise, from the verified disposable repository, restore the supplied bug with git restore --source baseline-bug --staged --worktree -- factorial.py test_factorial.py. Never run recovery in another repository.

sections.title: Create the disposable repository safely in PowerShell 7
paragraphs: Open PowerShell 7. The following script first verifies Git and selects a working Python 3 command. It prefers python when that command runs Python 3 and otherwise falls back to the Windows launcher command py -3. It then chooses a folder under your temporary directory and throws an error before creating or entering it if that exact path already exists. It creates both complete files with literal here-strings, initializes Git, and sets an explicit identity only in this repository. The git config commands omit --global intentionally.

The intentional defect is concrete: factorial uses n == 1 as its only base case. factorial(1) and factorial(5) work, but factorial(0) calls factorial(-1). The existing n < 0 guard then immediately raises ValueError with the message n must be non-negative. Do not repair the defect yet.

code.label: Verify prerequisites, create a new fixture, and commit the baseline

sections.title: No-model learner task
paragraphs: Run the setup exactly once. The final command should return a nonzero status, which is expected evidence rather than a setup failure. Its traceback should show ValueError: n must be non-negative for the zero case. Read factorial.py and test_factorial.py. Explain why only the zero case fails. Then change only factorial.py so zero and one are both terminating base cases. Do not alter test_factorial.py and do not copy the answer key until you have attempted the repair.

Use the same verified Python 3 command selected during setup. If you open a new PowerShell session, run the selection block below again. A correct result has one changed line in factorial.py, no test-file change, and three passing tests. Commit only after reviewing the diff and seeing the tests pass.

code.label: Manual review, verification, and controlled commit

sections.title: Expected result and verification
paragraphs: Before the repair, unittest should report test_factorial_of_zero as ERROR and include a traceback ending with ValueError: n must be non-negative. This happens because factorial(0) calls factorial(-1), and the explicit negative-input guard raises before another recursive call can occur. The run should report Ran 3 tests and end with FAILED (errors=1). The tests for one and five should report ok. If all tests pass before you edit, compare both files with the fixture because the intentional bug is absent.

After the repair, all three named tests should report ok, followed by Ran 3 tests and OK. The elapsed time is machine-dependent and is represented below as a pattern rather than a promised figure. A successful unittest run exits with status zero. Git status should be empty after the controlled commit. If factorial_of_one fails, you changed the base case incorrectly. If factorial_of_five fails, inspect the recursive return expression. If test_factorial.py appears in git diff, restore that file rather than weakening the tests.

code.label: Expected initial failing output pattern
code.code:
test_factorial_of_five (test_factorial.FactorialTests.test_factorial_of_five) ... ok
test_factorial_of_one (test_factorial.FactorialTests.test_factorial_of_one) ... ok
test_factorial_of_zero (test_factorial.FactorialTests.test_factorial_of_zero) ... ERROR
...

paragraphs: unittest may order discovered test methods alphabetically. The important checks are the three ok results, the count of three tests, and final OK.

sections.title: Optional, metered and unexecuted Aider path
paragraphs: This path is optional and was not executed to produce this resource. A hosted provider may charge for API usage. A local Ollama run avoids a hosted model API but still consumes local compute and requires Ollama plus a capable model that you have selected and pulled. Do not assume that any option is free or equally capable. Aider warns that less capable models can fail to return usable code edits.

If Aider is not already installed, the documented isolated installer path is python -m pip install aider-install followed by aider-install. When py -3 is the verified Python command, use py -3 -m pip install aider-install instead. Run aider --version and record its actual output locally. The exact current version is UNKNOWN in this card because the supplied evidence does not establish it. Installing software changes the user's Python or tool environment, so obtain approval first.

Start the optional run only after the manual solution is committed. The script below verifies the exact disposable repository path, requires a clean worktree and index, refuses a detached HEAD, refuses an existing aider-practice branch, and creates that named branch directly from baseline-bug. This keeps the manual solution on its original branch and reproducibly places the optional branch at the supplied bug without resetting or changing any global configuration. The final test command must be observed locally before launching Aider. It should fail with the zero-case ValueError. If it passes or fails differently, stop and inspect the fixture.

code.label: Install optionally, then create a clean practice branch from the bug

sections.title: Choose one documented provider without persisting secrets
paragraphs: DeepSeek setup below uses DEEPSEEK_API_KEY, as documented by Aider. The SecureString conversion places plain text in the current process environment because command-line programs require that form, but it avoids echoing or saving the key. Close the PowerShell process after the exercise and remove the variable as shown. Never commit an environment file.

The launch uses --no-auto-commits for this bounded exercise. Aider normally commits edits automatically, but this option leaves its edits pending so you can review and test them before deciding whether to use /commit. Launch only from the verified aider-practice branch created in the optional setup. The commands do not print the environment, Git configuration, or remote URLs.

sections.title: Run a bounded Aider edit, review, test, and recover
paragraphs: The launch command explicitly adds only factorial.py and test_factorial.py to the chat. Aider documentation recommends adding only needed files. At the Aider prompt, paste the complete request below. This is an instruction to a future optional run, not a transcript. No response or patch is predicted.

Aider normally commits each edit automatically. The provider commands in this exercise use --no-auto-commits so the learner can review and test pending edits first. Inside Aider, /diff shows changes since the preceding message. The /test command runs a child shell command and adds its output to the chat only when that command exits nonzero. Because that child shell cannot use the parent PowerShell variables or aliases, enter one literal test command chosen from the next section according to the executable you already verified.

Use /commit only if Git status shows pending changes, only factorial.py changed, the diff is understood, and the full test suite passes. The /commit command commits all dirty changes with a sensible message, so stop instead if any file outside the allowed scope is dirty. If you omit --no-auto-commits in another run, Aider may already have committed its edits automatically. In that case, do not run /commit merely to follow the sequence. Inspect /diff and /git show --stat --oneline HEAD instead. Aider marks commits it authored with (aider) in author and committer metadata by default. The /undo command applies only when the last commit was made by Aider. Never claim a commit or test passed without inspecting the actual local evidence.

code.label: Focused request to paste at the Aider prompt
code.code: Fix the intentional boundary bug in factorial.py so factorial(0) returns 1 while factorial(1) remains 1 and factorial(5) remains 120. Edit only factorial.py. Do not edit, remove, skip, or weaken test_factorial.py. Do not add dependencies or files. Preserve the existing TypeError and ValueError validation. Make the smallest clear change. After editing, stop so I can review the diff and run python -m unittest -v.

sections.title: In-chat review and controlled commit
paragraphs: Use this sequence only after launching with --no-auto-commits. Enter /diff first. For /test, choose exactly one literal command based on the Python 3 executable verified in PowerShell: use the python form if python was selected, or the py -3 form if the launcher fallback was selected. Do not enter both, and do not reference $PythonExe, $PythonArgs, a PowerShell function, or an alias because Aider runs the test in a child shell.

After the test passes, inspect status. Continue only if factorial.py is the sole changed file and test_factorial.py is unchanged. Run /commit only when those pending changes exist. If status is already clean, an automatic or external commit may already have occurred, so inspect the log and do not create an unnecessary commit. Aider's /test adds output to the chat on a nonzero exit; independently inspect the command result rather than assuming silence proves the requested behavior.

code.label: Aider in-chat commands with an explicit Python choice
code.code:
/diff

# Choose exactly one of the following based on the verified executable:
/test python -B -m unittest -v
# OR
/test py -3 -B -m unittest -v

/git status --short

# Only if factorial.py is the sole pending change and all tests passed:
/commit fix: handle zero factorial base case

/git status --short
/git log --oneline --decorate -2
/exit

sections.title: Safe recovery inside this disposable repository
paragraphs: Stop immediately if a credential appears in chat or a file, the model requests broader access, files outside scope change, tests are weakened, the diff is unclear, or verification fails. Press Control-C to interrupt an unhelpful response. Exit Aider before using the PowerShell recovery. The recovery script verifies both the disposable path and repository root, requires the named practice branch, and rejects changes or untracked files outside the two fixture files. It does not print environment variables, Git configuration, remote URLs, or file contents that might expose credentials.

The scoped git restore command restores only factorial.py and test_factorial.py in the index and worktree from baseline-bug. It does not reset a branch, detach HEAD, rewrite history, remove untracked files, change global configuration, or affect another repository. The verification test should again fail with ValueError: n must be non-negative for the zero case. That nonzero result is evidence that the supplied bug was restored, not a passing solution.

code.label: Restore the committed buggy checkpoint and verify it safely

sections.title: Answer key for the main task
paragraphs: Compare this answer only after attempting the task. The smallest successful patch changes the base-case comparison from equality with one to less than or equal to one. The existing negative-input guard runs first, so this broader base case does not accept negative integers. Zero now returns 1 directly, one still returns 1, and larger values recurse toward the base case.

code.label: Successful patch
code.code:
diff --git a/factorial.py b/factorial.py
--- a/factorial.py
+++ b/factorial.py
@@
-    if n == 1:  # Intentional bug: zero is also a base case.
+    if n <= 1:  # Zero and one are factorial base cases.
         return 1

sections.title: Variation: add explicit invalid-input tests
paragraphs: Start this variation only after the main repair passes and is committed. The concrete task is to add two tests without changing factorial.py: factorial(-1) must raise ValueError with the exact message n must be non-negative, and factorial(2.5) must raise TypeError with the exact message n must be an integer. Add the complete methods shown below inside FactorialTests and before the if __name__ block, then run the full suite. This variation practices specifying exceptions and preserving an already-correct implementation.

Each method first uses assertRaises to capture the required exception object. It then compares str(caught.exception) with the complete expected string using assertEqual. This is a literal string equality check, so additional prefixes, suffixes, punctuation, or whitespace cause the test to fail. Expected success is five ok tests, Ran 5 tests, and OK. If the required exception type is not raised, inspect the implementation's guards. If the string comparison fails, compare the actual and expected messages. If discovery reports only three tests, inspect indentation and placement.

code.label: Complete learner variation methods to add inside FactorialTests
code.code:
def test_negative_integer_is_rejected(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError) as caught:
            factorial(-1)
        self.assertEqual(str(caught.exception), "n must be non-negative")

    def test_non_integer_is_rejected(self):
        with self.assertRaises(TypeError) as caught:
            factorial(2.5)
        self.assertEqual(str(caught.exception), "n must be an integer")

sections.title: Explained solution for the variation
paragraphs: The two tests use unittest's exception context manager to capture exceptions. assertRaises requires the specified exception type. The following assertEqual compares the exception's complete string representation with one literal expected message, which makes the message check genuinely exact rather than a regular-expression match. No production-code change is needed because the fixture checks type before numeric range and rejects negative integers. A bool is also rejected by the existing explicit isinstance(n, bool) check, although that input is outside this variation.

After inserting both complete methods inside FactorialTests, review the diff and run the full suite with the verified Python 3 command. Commit only test_factorial.py because factorial.py should remain unchanged. If verification fails or factorial.py changed, restore both files from HEAD. That recovery is safe here because the main solution was committed before starting the variation.

code.label: Verify, commit, or recover the variation

sections.title: Evidence boundaries and assumptions
paragraphs: The source pages were checked on 2026-09-19 as documentation evidence, not as evidence that any command in this card was executed. Expected unittest output is a pattern derived from the complete fixture. With the supplied negative-input guard, factorial(0) calls factorial(-1), and that call raises ValueError: n must be non-negative before further recursion. Exact traceback formatting, method qualification, and elapsed time vary by Python version and environment.

ASSUMPTIONS. PowerShell 7 and a writable temporary directory are available. Python 3 is approved and available through either python or the Windows py -3 launcher. Git is approved and available through git. The learner starts the initial setup with no path named aider-factorial-lab in the temporary directory. Before the optional path, the learner has committed the manual solution and has no existing local branch named aider-practice. Optional installation, provider terms, billing, data policy, Ollama installation, and local model suitability are reviewed by the learner or organization before use.

OMITTED. No actual Aider or model execution, deterministic model response, literal credential, current Aider version, or universal Ollama model ID is supplied. Those would be unsupported or unsafe given the supplied evidence. No requested core exercise component is omitted.
